title: Probabilistic cradle‐to‐gate carbon footprint of e‐methanol under coupled electricity and CO2‐source conditions: Comparison with published projects and an industrial‐park application
content:
Abstract

Electricity supply, CO2 sourcing and process heat determine whether e-methanol has a lower cradle-to-gate carbon footprint than fossil methanol. We developed a screening model for 1 kg methanol and propagated uncertainty in four foreground parameters using Monte Carlo analysis. Against a natural-gas-methanol reference of 0.944 kg CO2e per kg of methanol, median break-even electricity factors were 0.075 and 0.053 kg CO2e/kWh for high-concentration and point-source CO2, with fifth-percentile (P5) thresholds of 0.069 and 0.048. Sampling residual heat over 0–4 MJ per kg of methanol lowered the point-source P5 threshold to 0.033. For the high-temperature direct-air-capture route, adding an illustrative U.S.-average upstream natural-gas burden lowered the break-even factor from 0.027 to 0.018 kg CO2e/kWh. In the 100,000 t/y park case, the 97% wind-equivalent, 100-km point-source configuration had a footprint of 0.921 kg CO2e per kg of methanol; lower capture-heat efficiency reversed its small advantage over the reference. These results identify electricity intensity, CO2 supply and heat integration as key variables for early-stage screening.
